input.title: Move LH-11 from TP-1250-02 to TP-1310-04 to cover failed LH-07

options.description: No reaction. TP-1310-04 (8.4 g/t) has no loader from 09:30 to 17:00 (7.5 h).
Hold and resume at likely repair time 14:30 (PR-0001; range 13:30-16:30). Loses 5 h at TP-1310-04. If the high case (16:30) occurs, the loss is 7 h = 210 t / 56.7 oz.
Move LH-11 from TP-1250-02 (4.1 g/t, lowest-grade, loading-only) to TP-1310-04. 1 h ramp move, on site 10:35. Loses 32.5 t at TP-1310-04 and 148.3 t at TP-1250-02.

Move LH-10 from TP-1310-11 (6.0 g/t, loading-only), same level, 0.5 h, on site 10:05. Loses 17.5 t at TP-1310-04 and 163.2 t at TP-1310-11. Net protected is only 24.5 oz because the donor's grade is higher, so it is worse than LH-11.

input.calculation: Rates assume a 10 h productive window (07:00-17:00). TP-1310-04: 300 t / 10 h = 30 t/h. TP-1250-02: 200 / 10 = 20 t/h. oz = t x g/t / 31.1035. Rules: LOADER-BACKUP-01 picks the lowest-grade stope as donor. LOADER-BACKUP-02 allows only phase 'carguio' donors, which excludes DF-1310-05, TP-1220-01, TP-1280-02 and TP-1310-07 (combined cycles). The eligible donors include TP-1250-02 at 4.1 g/t, the lowest of all stopes. MOVE-TIME-01: a 1250 to 1310 ramp move takes 1 h. Failure at 09:18, loss counted from 09:30 when repair started. Decision is at about 09:35, so LH-11 arrives at 10:35. do_nothing: 7.5 h x 30 = 225 t x 8.4 / 31.1035 = 60.8 oz. wait_for_repair: 09:30 to 14:30 = 5 h x 30 = 150 t = 40.5 oz. reassign LH-11: the gap at 1310-04 from 09:30 to 10:35 is 1.083 h x 30 = 32.5 t = 8.8 oz. Protected: 6.417 h x 30 = 192.5 t x 8.4 / 31.1035 = 52.0 oz. Lost at TP-1250-02 from 09:35 to 17:00: 7.417 h x 20 = 148.3 t x 4.1 / 31.1035 = 19.5 oz. Net = 52.0 - 19.5 = 32.4 oz. Total at risk = 180.8 t, 28.3 oz, which is 32.5 oz better than do_nothing and 12.2 oz better than waiting. LH-10 alternative: it is on the same level (0.5 h, arrives 10:05), the gap at the stope is 17.5 t = 4.7 oz, and protected is 207.5 t = 56.0 oz. Lost at TP-1310-11 is 7.417 h x 22 t/h = 163.2 t x 6.0 / 31.1035 = 31.5 oz. Net = 24.5 oz, lower than LH-11. Other donors (LH-05 5.8 g/t, LH-08 5.5 g/t) have higher grade than LH-11's stope, so their net is lower. Upside not counted: once LH-07 is repaired (about 14:30 likely), LH-11 could return to TP-1250-02, which would recover some of the 19.5 oz. This requires another 1 h move and a decision at that time. The calculation conservatively keeps LH-11 at 1310-04 to 17:00.

content.text:
I submitted proposal PR-0002 for approval: move LH-11 from TP-1250-02 to TP-1310-04 to cover the failed LH-07, starting by 09:35. It nets about 32.4 oz protected, and my confidence is 0.7 because the repair time is unconfirmed.

- **Do nothing:** loses 225 t and 60.8 oz at TP-1310-04.
- **Wait for repair:** the likely repair finishes at 14:30, which loses 150 t and 40.5 oz.
- **Move LH-11:** TP-1250-02 is the lowest-grade loading-only stope, at 4.1 g/t. The ramp move to 1310 takes 1 h. It protects 192.5 t and 52.0 oz at TP-1310-04 and loses 148.3 t and 19.5 oz at TP-1250-02. Total at risk drops to 180.8 t and 28.3 oz.
- **Move LH-10 instead:** the same-level move is faster, but the net is only 24.5 oz because the donor stope grades 6.0 g/t.

I kept LH-11 at 1310-04 until 17:00. Sending it back after LH-07 is repaired could recover some of the 19.5 oz, but I did not count that.

The repair time is still a crew guess by sound (4–7 h). Someone should check the inspection result, spare pump availability and whether the ramp to 1310 is clear.
